Exercise A

Before You Write: Precision, Register & Reporting

Every option below is grammatically correct. Choose the one you would actually send to a colleague or a customer.

Choose the better version
These eight habits are what your writing in Exercise B is judged on: say when, ask instead of demand, report accurately, hedge what you have not confirmed, commit to a time, drop the jargon for a non-technical reader, and close with a clear request.
1. Reporting when something failed: “The backup job failed ”
2. Asking a user for something you need:
3. Summarising what the user told you: “She said that the error every time she opened the file.”
4. Naming a cause you have not yet confirmed: “The outage have been caused by last night's update.”
5. Committing to a timeframe: “I will update you ”
6. Explaining a delay to a reader who is not technical: “The migration was postponed because ”
7. Recording an action in a report: “The affected accounts before 09:00.”
8. Closing a message that needs the reader to do something:
